title: The artifact cache's directory has one spelling, `opcache.file_cache_dir`, and `[cache]` holds `Core\Cache`'s two tiers and nothing else
scope:
which of two parsed keys names the directory compiled artifacts are read from, and what
happens to a file that writes the other one. It changes nothing about the cache's layout, how an
entry is verified before it is mapped, the ownership check on the directory, or either
`Core\Cache` tier.
validatedBy:
`crates/nvs-config/tests/directives.rs`, `crates/nvs-config/tests/snapshot.rs`,
`crates/nvs-config/tests/request.rs`, `crates/nvs-config/tests/tree.rs`,
`tests/conformance/core/config-unconfigured-host-answers-as-an-empty-configuration.nvst`, and
`python tools/directives.py --check`, which fails on any leaf key that reaches no reader.

summary.headline: The compile cache directory has one spelling; `[cache]` is the value cache
summary.body:
`opcache.file_cache_dir` is where compiled programs are cached, and it is the only key that says
so. `[cache] dir` used to parse and be read by nobody, so an operator who set it moved nothing
and was told nothing; writing it now is an unknown-directive error naming the file and line.
`[cache]` holds the settings of `Core\Cache`'s local and shared tiers and nothing else. Changing
the compile cache directory takes a restart; the rest of `[opcache]` is read at the next
compile.
